fact: Firestone's code requires artificial turf blade colors to mimic natural turf, with green blade colors and a tan thatch layer, a bender board, curb or similar border that conceals the turf's edges, and turf kept looking like healthy living turf.
quote: d. Appearance. i. Blade yarn colors shall mimic natural turf including green blade color(s) and include a tan thatch layer. … vi. Artificial turf shall be separated from other landscape areas by a bender board, concrete curbing or similar material to conceal edges of the turf. f. Maintenance. i. Artificial turf shall be maintained in a manner to mimic healthy living turf. ii. Artificial turf shall be cleaned as necessary and groomed to maintain its appearance.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.d.i, F.2.e.vi and F.2.f.i–ii (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through the Municode content API (jobId 488870, productId 18062, node TIT16FIDECO_CH6DEDEST_16.6.4LASCFE), the text the library page renders. The same F.2 section carries the pile, face-weight, base and permit rules in the shared city-codes records; does-artificial-turf-fade and artificial-turf-edging-options quote parts of this text too. Applies to existing single-family lots (16.6.1.B, per firestone-fdc-16.6.4-permit).

fact: CSU Extension's PlantTalk Colorado says Kentucky bluegrass is the most widely used lawn grass in Colorado.
quote: Kentucky bluegrass is a good choice for many situations and uses. It’s the most widely used lawn grass in Colorado.
source_label: PlantTalk Colorado 1521, Choosing a Lawn Grass in Colorado (CSU Extension)

fact: CSU Extension says Kentucky bluegrass has long been the standard lawn because of its dense stand, rich bluish green color and wear tolerance, and that most new Colorado lawns are simply assumed to be bluegrass.
quote: Kentucky bluegrass, Poa pratensis, has been a standard for the beautiful green lawn since the days of King Louis of France due to its dense stand, rich bluish green color, and wear tolerance. … The basic assumption is that Kentucky bluegrass must be planted, and little consideration is given to alternative turfgrass species.
source_label: CSU Extension, CMG GardenNotes #561, Turfgrass Species Selection Guidelines (Koski)

fact: CSU Extension says buffalograss and blue grama, the warm-season lawn grasses, turn straw-colored with the first fall frost and don't green up again until late spring, around May.
quote: Warm season grass; becomes straw-colored with first hard fall frost and begins to green up in mid to late May. … Warm season grass that becomes straw-colored with first frost in fall, greening up in late spring (May)
source_label: CSU Extension, CMG GardenNotes #561, Turfgrass Species Selection Guidelines: Buffalograss and Blue Grama
notes: The first sentence is under Buffalograss (Disadvantages), the second under Blue Grama (Disadvantages), both on page 561-5 of the PDF.

fact: CSU Extension describes lawn thatch as a tight, brown, spongy layer of living and dead roots and stems above the soil, and says it tends to build up in Kentucky bluegrass lawns.
quote: Thatch is a tight, brown, spongy, organic layer of both living and dead grass roots and stems that accumulates above the soil surface. … Grass species – Thatch tends to be a problem on Kentucky bluegrass, bentgrass, and fine fescue lawns.
source_label: CSU Extension, CMG GardenNotes #551, Basic Turf Management: Thatch

fact: CSU Extension's PlantTalk Colorado says Kentucky bluegrass can survive long periods without irrigation because of its excellent dormancy mechanism.
quote: Second, it can survive well for extended periods of time without any irrigation due to its excellent dormancy mechanism.
source_label: PlantTalk Colorado 1540, Drought Tolerance of Kentucky Bluegrass (CSU Extension)

fact: CSU Extension's PlantTalk Colorado writes of dormant bluegrass lawns as brown, including lawns that stay dormant and brown for a month or more.
quote: Fall fertilization of dormant (brown) lawns, especially those that have been dormant (brown) a month or more, will provide little or no benefit this fall (although spring green-up of dormant, still-living bluegrass lawns will be enhanced.)
source_label: PlantTalk Colorado 1535, Fall Lawn Fertilization: During Drought (CSU Extension)

fact: CSU Extension says Colorado often has little or no snow cover from October through March, and that the low angle of winter sun sharpens reflected-heat effects on south and west exposures.
quote: Often there is little or no snow cover to provide soil moisture from October through March. … Plants receiving reflected heat from buildings, walls, and fences are more subject to damage. The low angle of winter sun makes this more likely on south or west exposures.
source_label: CSU Extension fact sheet 7.211, Fall and Winter Watering of Plants and Trees (Klett and Cox; reviewed August 2025)

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's buying guidelines say longer, denser synthetic grass generally looks more natural, and tell buyers to choose landscape turf that replicates the grass varieties most common where they live.
quote: Generally, longer pile and denser synthetic grass will look more natural. … Guidelines to Assure a Natural Appearance Select landscape synthetic grass that replicates the grass varieties that are most prevalent in your locality.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)
notes: Read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25. "Guidelines to Assure a Natural Appearance" is the section heading on page 4; the pile sentence is under Total Yarn Weight (aka Face Weight) on page 3. The same document is cited by does-artificial-turf-fade for its UV test minimums.

fact: SYNLawn's installation guidelines say artificial grass has a grain, that every piece in an area should share one grain direction facing the way the lawn is seen most often, and that sand brushed into the turf helps the fibers stand upright.
quote: When designing, always keep the grain direction the same and try to face it toward the direction it will be seen most often. … Note: Like other textile products, artificial grass has a grain direction. It is important to remember to keep the same grain direction for all pieces installed in the same area. … The sand will help support the fibers to stand upright.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (PDF posted with the product listing)
notes: The manufacturer's own PDF, hosted on the retailer's product-document server; the same document other guides cite. Read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25.

fact: Integriturf's installation guide says turf looks richest in color, with the least sheen, when you look into its grain, so a front yard's grain usually leans toward the street; that pieces seamed with mismatched grain show a color difference; and that brushing against the grain helps fibers stand up and look more natural.
quote: Most turf products have a grain that leans in one direction. The best side to view the turf would be looking into the grain (for example: if you are installing turf in your front yard, you would typically have the grain lean towards the street so that people facing the house from the street would be looking into the grain that is leaning towards the street. Looking into the grain typically provides the best color and least amount of sheen. … If you seam sections together without keeping the consistent grain direction you will notice a color difference and seams will be visible. … Use a power broom to brush the turf fibers in the opposite direction of the grain. This will help the fibers stand up and look more natural
notes: Integriturf is a turf supplier; its guide is a general overview for homeowners and installers. Read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, a turf distributor, says manufacturers developed varied blade shapes to reduce plastic sheen, and describes its S-shaped blade as reflecting less sunlight and its corrugated blade as reducing shine.
quote: With time and technology advances, manufacturers have developed more lifelike products with varying blade shapes to reduce the plastic sheen and increase the visual volume. … The “S” Blade is built utilizing an S’s curves to reflect less sunlight – giving it a more natural and realistic appearance. … The intricate shape also reduces shine and creates a more visual texture and depth in each blade
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse (SGW), About Blade Shapes
notes: A seller's description of its own products' blade shapes; copy presents it as a maker's claim to test with a sample, not as a measured result.

fact: ForeverLawn's Select LX specification lists field and olive green for its primary yarn and turf green and dark tan for its secondary yarn, tufted in the same row.
quote: Color: Primary: Field/olive green; Secondary: Turf green/dark tan … Construction: Dual yarn, same row
notes: Read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25, section 2.1.A. The sheet does not name a blade shape. An example of how a spec sheet lists color, not a recommendation.

fact: SYNLawn's SYNAugustine 847 spec sheet lists sport green, apple and olive for the grass-zone yarn, field green and beige for the thatch-zone yarn, and a Biomimetic U blade shape.
quote: SYNAUGUSTINE 847 A robust and highly durable artificial turf with a low pile height, tightly knit thatch, and realistic grass blades … Grass Zone Yarn/Color PE / Sport Green/Apple/Olive … Thatch Zone Yarn/Color PE / Field Green/Beige … Grass Zone Yarn Shape Biomimetic™ U
notes: Read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25. An example of how a spec sheet lists color, not a recommendation.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's page for TigerTurf Majestic lists field green, lime green and tan blade colors, a green and tan thatch, and two blade shapes, a 3D curvy W and an oval.
quote: Majestic's 3D Curvy “W” and Oval turf blades … While showcasing field green, lime green, and tan color combinations, Majestic also features a life-like green and tan thatch to emulate a natural grass lawn best. … Colors: Field Green / Lime Green / Tan … Thatch Color: Green & Tan
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse (SGW), TigerTurf Majestic product page
notes: Read 2026-09-25 (product description and Product Specifications). An example of how a spec sheet lists color, not a recommendation.
